project_specification.project_name: nullius — a tail-decile research book: long the top decile, short the bottom decile, equal-weight within legs
project_specification.addition_summary:
docs/preregistration/2026-10-19-h5-repricing.RESULT.md found that the horizon-5 reversal picks rank the cross-section out of sample (portfolio rank IC t +2.45 on 239 names) while neither the z-weighted nor the inverse-volatility dollar-neutral book earns anything gross. An in-sample decile diagnostic on the wide snapshot (scratchpad/decile_diag.py, six picks, 61 weekly dates) shows why: the forward-return gradient sits in the bottom decile (−63 to −73 bp per 5-day period for the volatility and borrow-proxy constructs) while deciles 2–10 are flat and non-monotone; the top-minus-bottom spread is +126 to +136 bp (t 2.0–2.4) where the proportional book earns +6 to +27 bp. A book proportional to score spreads its gross over eight deciles that carry no gradient.
This addition gives the research book a third weighting, "tail_decile": each date's book is long the top decile of scores and short the bottom decile, equal-weight within each leg, dollar-neutral, gross 1, with the existing beta-neutral rescale applied after. It sits at the same seam as inverse_vol and leaves every default untouched; the nightly evaluation canary enforces that the default path still reproduces its frozen score.

category.name: Research Book
category.feature:
System lets the evaluation config set book.weighting to "tail_decile", under which each date's research book is long the top decile of scores and short the bottom decile, equal-weight within each leg, dollar-neutral and gross 1, with the beta-neutral rescale applied after, so that a ranking whose return gradient lives in its tails is traded where the gradient is (the dream cycle summary displays the weighting in force, and a cross-section too small for two non-empty deciles is refused for that date with an error message naming the date and the count).
- book_weights gains a keyword-only weighting: str = "z" (closed vocabulary {"z", "inverse_vol", "tail_decile"}; "inverse_vol" is what vols= not None means today and the two must agree or be refused by name). For "tail_decile": sort the scored symbols by score ascending with ties broken by symbol name; the bottom decile is the first floor(n/10) names and the top decile the last floor(n/10), each needing at least 2 names (else refuse with EvaluatorMetricsError naming the date's count); long leg weights +0.5/k_top each, short leg −0.5/k_bottom each, every other name 0.0; then the existing beta-neutral rescale when betas is given. vols is ignored under "tail_decile". With weighting "z" the function is byte-for-byte today's behaviour. - compute_node_metrics gains the same keyword-only weighting and passes it through per date; the rank IC is unchanged (still over the full joined cross-section). NodeMetrics gains tail_k: Mapping[date, int] (default empty) recording k per date under tail_decile. - BookConfig's weighting vocabulary gains "tail_decile" (TAIL_DECILE_WEIGHTING constant); both evaluation chains pass weighting=context.book.weighting to compute_node_metrics (and compute vols only for inverse_vol, as today). The dream cycle summary already displays the weighting (2d2f9c48); confirm it shows "tail_decile". - Tests (new files): a 20-name fixture gives exactly 2 longs at +0.25 and 2 shorts at −0.25 with gross 1 and net 0, with ties broken by name; a 50-name fixture gives 5 and 5 at ±0.1; a 15-name cross-section (floor 1.5 = 1 per leg) is refused naming the count; betas compose after the legs are formed (compare with _beta_neutral_weights applied to the tail weights); weighting "z" reproduces an existing fixture's weights and compute_node_metrics output to 1e-12; "inverse_vol" with vols reproduces the existing inverse-vol test expectations; the config parses "tail_decile", refuses an unknown value, and the evaluation chain under "tail_decile" produces per-date books equal to book_weights(scores, betas, weighting="tail_decile") on a fixture. The evaluator and orchestrator tests touched pass.
